description: Warp padding broadens the inherited unguarded frequency-read concern and introduces unguarded normalization-weight reads for padded lanes.
trigger: Use a head dimension not divisible by 64, such as the new 80-wide test, or use partial rotary frequencies shorter than the launched x dimension.
expected_behavior: Inactive lanes avoid frequency and weight reads outside their logical arrays.
actual_behavior: All x threads read inv_freq[t], and normalization reads a half2 weight without a head-width guard. For D=80, 64 threads address a 40-element full-width frequency array and 128 half-weight elements despite an 80-element norm vector. The shared activation load is padded, but these input arrays are not.

finding.description: Inherited native reduction and padded-input-read concerns are carried over.
finding.trigger: Direct fused RoPE normalization with nonuniform lane values; or rotation with padded head width, such as 80, or shorter partial-rotary frequencies.
finding.expected_behavior: Store one complete sum per warp and avoid input reads beyond logical frequency/weight arrays.
finding.actual_behavior: Every lane writes its shuffle-down result to one shared sum slot. inv_freq[t] and normalization half2 weight loads lack padding guards. The existing test directly reaches this kernel with width 80 and normalization on/off, bypassing Attention's new dispatch failure. LayerNorm avoids the normalization-specific operations but not the frequency read.

finding.description: Warp-padded threads still read frequencies and normalization weights without logical-width guards; table lookup inherits this issue.
finding.trigger: Use head_dim=80, present in the existing tests, or a vector shorter than the launched rotary-thread width.
finding.expected_behavior: Inactive lanes avoid reading beyond frequency rows and norm-weight arrays.
finding.actual_behavior: The launch rounds 40 channel pairs to 64 threads. All threads read frequencies before the rotary-width guard; table mode can cross into the next row or beyond the final row. With fused normalization, padded lanes also read half2 norm weights beyond the 80-element vector. These reads remain reachable through RoPE.apply and the three Attention routes.
